page: Amazon Web Services h1.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance tailored for applications requiring dense local storage capacity and parallel compute. It is powered by Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processors operating at 2.3 GHz under the Xen hypervisor, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system features 256 GB of DDR memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, alongside 45 MB of L3 cache. Storage consists of a bundled 16,000 GB local HDD array without GPU acceleration, complemented by a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a pronounced contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core performance metrics in stress-ng and Geekbench place in the lower 10 percent of evaluated systems, a consequence of the older Broadwell microarchitecture and conservative 2.3 GHz base frequency. In contrast, parallel scaling proves robust: multi-core stress-ng scores achieve average tier status at 30,599.75, and PassMark database operations benchmark in the upper quartile at 22,729.85. Memory subsystem metrics yield standard throughput under cached conditions at 2,304.47 GB/sec, though uncached large-block write speeds scale down to 44.1 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the h1.16xlarge centers on compute recency versus local capacity. While lacking advanced vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 and showing low per-core throughput in code compilation and compression, it supplies massive magnetic storage density directly attached to the host. This configuration delivers favorable resource density for bulk data persistence and sequential disk operations compared to solid-state alternatives. The server aligns with distributed file systems, MapReduce analytics, Apache Kafka broker nodes, log ingestion clusters, and batch ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services h1.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance designed for data-intensive processing and high sequential disk throughput. Built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processors running at 2.3 GHz, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, accompanied by 256 GB of system memory, a 25 Gbps baseline network interface, and 16,000 GB of bundled local HDD storage without GPU acceleration. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core processing performance, highlighted by strong database operations in PassMark testing and solid parallel decompression throughput. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks register in the lowest tier, reflecting the older CPU generation and moderate clock speed. The server trades per-core execution speed for large local magnetic storage capacity and multi-threaded parallelism. Its architecture targets distributed file systems, Hadoop or MapReduce clusters, batch data ingestion, and bulk sequential data pipelines.
